evidence: M-O s.v. school types: university, after Egger
terms.comment: Classically ūniversitās is the whole, and in the jurists a corporation (Gai. Inst. 2.11, Lewis & Short); the guilds of masters and students that became the universities took the name in the Middle Ages. Studiōrum makes the sense plain; Traupman also allows ūniversitās alone.

evidence: M-O s.v. school types: university, after Vives (1540), Mercator (1595) and Tursellinus (1652)
terms.comment: The humanists’ word for a university. Classically the gymnasium outside Athens where Plato taught, and the name Cicero gave to his villa near Puteoli and to a gymnasium at his Tusculan villa (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: in Valentīnā Acadēmīā (ūniversitātem vocant) tōtō orbe celeberrimā
phrases.english: at the Academy of Valencia (they call it a university), the most famous in the whole world
phrases.source: Ruiz (1794), p. viii, quoted by Morgan–Owens s.v. school types: university

academia.html: Cicero’s own verse scans it long: Inque Acadēmīā umbriferā nitidōque Lycēō (Div. 1.22), where -dēmī- makes a spondee before the elided final -ā. Lewis & Short: long in Cicero and in Tullius Laurea (ap. Plin. NH 31.8), short only in Claudian and Sidonius. Greek Ἀκαδήμεια.
